translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Tai sent Grand General Zhao Gui to command southeastern provincial troops to the rescue; from north of Changshe onward all became marshland, and the army reached Xiang but could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Tai sent Grand General Zhao Gui to command southeastern provincial troops to the rescue; from north of Changshe onward all became marshland, and the army reached Xiang but could not advance.

sentences.zh: 東魏人使善射者乘大艦臨城射之，城垂陷；

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei men had skilled archers aboard large ships shoot at the city from close range; the city was near collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei put skilled archers aboard large ships to shoot at the city from close range; the city was near collapse.

sentences.zh: 燕郡景惠公慕容紹宗與劉豐生臨堰視之，見東北塵起，同入艦坐避之。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong, Duke of Jinghui of Yanz commandery, and Liu Fengsheng came to the dam to observe; seeing dust rise in the northeast, they both entered a ship and sat to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong, Duke of Jinghui of Yanz commandery, and Liu Fengsheng came to the dam to observe; seeing dust rise in the northeast, they both boarded a ship to take shelter.

sentences.zh: 俄而暴風至，遠近晦冥，纜斷，飄船徑向城；

translations.literal: Soon a violent wind came; near and far turned dark; mooring lines snapped; the drifting ship headed straight for the city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a violent wind came; near and far turned dark; mooring lines snapped; the drifting ship headed straight for the city.

sentences.zh: 城上人以長鉤牽船，弓弩亂髮，紹宗赴水溺死，豐生游上，向土山，城上人射殺之。

translations.literal: Men on the wall hooked the ship with long poles; bows and crossbows fired in disorder; Shaozong threw himself into the water and drowned; Fengsheng swam ashore toward an earthen hill and was shot dead by men on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the wall hooked the ship with long poles; bows and crossbows fired in a storm; Shaozong threw himself into the water and drowned; Fengsheng swam ashore toward an earthen hill and was shot dead by the defenders.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，東魏進大將軍勃海王澄位相國，封齊王，加殊禮。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Eastern Wei promoted Grand General Cheng, Prince of Bohai, to Chancellor of State, enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi, and granted extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Eastern Wei promoted Grand General Gao Cheng, Prince of Bohai, to Chancellor of State, enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi, and granted extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 丁未，澄入朝於鄴，固辭；

translations.literal: On dingwei, Cheng entered court at Ye and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Cheng entered court at Ye and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: They would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: They would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 澄召將佐密議之，皆勸澄宜膺朝命，獨散騎常侍陳元康以為未可，澄由是嫌之。

translations.literal: Cheng summoned his generals and aides for secret counsel; all urged him to accept the court's command; only Direct Attendant Chen Yuankang thought it premature, and Cheng therefore came to dislike him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng summoned his generals and aides for secret counsel; all urged him to accept the court's command; only Direct Attendant Chen Yuankang thought it premature, and Cheng therefore came to dislike him.

sentences.zh: 崔暹乃薦陸元規為大行台郎以分元康之權。

translations.literal: Cui Xian then recommended Lu Yuangui as an officer of the Grand Mobile Headquarters to divide Yuankang's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian then recommended Lu Yuangui as an officer of the Grand Mobile Headquarters to divide Yuankang's authority.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹之入援也，令所督諸州皆發兵，雍州刺史岳陽王察遣府司馬劉方貴將兵出漢口；

translations.literal: When Prince Yi of Xiangdong marched to the rescue, he ordered all provinces under his command to raise troops; Yongzhou Inspector Prince Cha of Yueyang sent his chief administrator Liu Fanggui with troops out from Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yi of Xiangdong marched to the rescue, he ordered all provinces under his command to raise troops; Yongzhou Inspector Prince Cha of Yueyang sent his chief administrator Liu Fanggui with troops out from Hankou.

sentences.zh: 繹召察使自行，察不從。

translations.literal: Yi summoned Cha to come in person; Cha refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yi summoned Cha to come in person; Cha refused.

sentences.zh: 方貴潛與繹相知，謀襲襄陽，未發；

translations.literal: Fanggui secretly communicated with Yi and plotted to strike Xiangyang, but had not yet acted.
translations.idiomatic: Fanggui secretly communicated with Yi and plotted to strike Xiangyang, but had not yet acted.

sentences.zh: 會察以它事召方貴，方貴以為謀洩，遂據樊城拒命，察遣軍攻之。

translations.literal: Just then Cha summoned Fanggui on another matter; Fanggui thought the plot had leaked, seized Fancheng and defied orders; Cha sent troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Cha summoned Fanggui on another matter; Fanggui thought the plot had leaked, seized Fancheng and defied orders; Cha sent troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 繹厚資遣張纘使赴鎮，纘至大堤，察已拔樊城，斬方貴。

translations.literal: Yi richly supplied Zhang Zuan and sent him to take up his post; Zuan reached Dadi; Cha had already taken Fancheng and beheaded Fanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Yi richly supplied Zhang Zuan and sent him to take up his post; Zuan reached Dadi; Cha had already taken Fancheng and beheaded Fanggui.

sentences.zh: 纘至襄陽，察推遷未去，但以城西白馬寺處之；

translations.literal: Zuan reached Xiangyang; Cha put off the transfer and did not leave, lodging Zuan only at White Horse Temple west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan reached Xiangyang; Cha put off the transfer and did not leave, lodging Zuan only at White Horse Temple west of the city.

sentences.zh: 察猶總軍府之政，聞台城陷，遂不受代。

translations.literal: Cha still controlled military affairs at headquarters; on hearing the capital had fallen, he refused to be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Cha still controlled military affairs at headquarters; on hearing the capital had fallen, he refused to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 助防杜岸紿纘曰：「觀岳陽勢不容使君，不如且往西山以避禍。

translations.literal: Assistant Defender Du An deceived Zuan, saying, "Judging Yueyang's posture, he will not tolerate you, my lord; better go for now to the western hills to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Defender Du An deceived Zuan: "Judging Yueyang's posture, he will not tolerate you; better go for now to the western hills to escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 」岸既襄陽豪族，兄弟九人，皆以驍勇著名。

translations.literal: " An was of a powerful Xiangyang clan; nine brothers, all famed for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: " An was of a powerful Xiangyang clan; nine brothers, all famed for fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 纘乃與岸結盟，著婦人衣，乘青布輿，逃入西山。

translations.literal: Zuan then allied with An, put on women's clothes, rode in a blue-cloth carriage, and fled into the western hills.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan then allied with An, put on women's clothes, rode in a blue-cloth carriage, and fled into the western hills.

sentences.zh: 察使岸將兵追擒之，纘乞為沙門，更名法纘，察許之。

translations.literal: Cha had An lead troops in pursuit and capture him; Zuan begged to become a monk, changed his name to Fazuan, and Cha consented.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had An lead troops in pursuit and capture him; Zuan begged to become a monk, changed his name to Fazuan, and Cha consented.

sentences.zh: 荊州長史王沖等上箋於湘東王繹，請以太尉、都督中外諸軍事承製主盟，繹不許。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Chief Administrator Wang Chong and others submitted a memorial to Prince Yi of Xiangdong, asking him to serve as Grand Commandant, Commander of All Forces Inside and Outside, assume regency, and lead the alliance; Yi refused.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou Chief Administrator Wang Chong and others submitted a memorial to Prince Yi of Xiangdong, asking him to serve as Grand Commandant, Commander of All Forces Inside and Outside, assume regency, and lead the alliance; Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，又請以司空主盟，亦不許。

translations.literal: On bingchen, they again asked him to lead the alliance as Minister of Works; again he refused.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, they again asked him to lead the alliance as Minister of Works; again he refused.

sentences.zh: 上雖外為侯景所制，而內甚不平。

translations.literal: Though outwardly controlled by Hou Jing, inwardly the emperor was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Though outwardly controlled by Hou Jing, inwardly the emperor was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 景欲以宋子仙為司空，上曰：「調和陰陽，安用此物！

translations.literal: Jing wished to make Song Zixian Minister of Works; the emperor said, "Harmonizing yin and yang—what use is there for such a creature!
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing wished to make Song Zixian Minister of Works; the emperor said, "Harmonizing yin and yang—what use is there for such a creature!

sentences.zh: 」景又請以其黨二人為便殿主帥，上不許。

translations.idiomatic: " Hou Jing again asked that two of his partisans be made commanders of the side halls; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 景不能強，心甚憚之。

translations.literal: Jing could not force the issue and inwardly feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing could not force the issue and inwardly feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 太子入，泣諫，上曰：「誰令汝來！

translations.literal: The crown prince entered and remonstrated through tears; the emperor said, "Who told you to come!
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince entered and remonstrated through tears; the emperor said, "Who told you to come!

sentences.zh: 若社稷有靈，猶當克復；

translations.literal: If the altars of state have spirit, we may yet recover;
translations.idiomatic: If the altars of state have spirit, we may yet recover;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，何事流涕！

translations.literal: if not, what use are tears!
translations.idiomatic: if not, what use are tears!

translations.literal: " Jing had his soldiers enter duty in the Secretariat; some drove donkeys and horses, carrying bows and blades, passing in and out of the palace grounds; the emperor wondered and asked; Direct Attendant General Zhou Shizhen answered, "Chancellor Hou's armored men.
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Jing had his soldiers enter duty in the Secretariat; some drove donkeys and horses, carrying bows and blades, passing in and out of the palace grounds; the emperor wondered and asked; Direct Attendant General Zhou Shizhen answered, "Chancellor Hou's armored men.

sentences.zh: 」上大怒，叱石珍曰：「是侯景，何謂丞相！

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angered and shouted at Shizhen, "That is Hou Jing—what do you mean, chancellor!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly angered and shouted at Shizhen, "That is Hou Jing—what do you mean, chancellor!

sentences.zh: 」左右皆懼。

translations.literal: " Those around him were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " Those around him were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 是後上所求多不遂志，飲膳亦為所裁節，憂憤成疾。

translations.literal: After this the emperor's requests mostly went unfulfilled; his food and drink were also curtailed; grief and anger became illness.
translations.idiomatic: After this the emperor's requests mostly went unfulfilled; his food and drink were also curtailed; grief and anger became illness.

sentences.zh: 太子以幼子大圜屬湘東王繹，並剪爪發以寄之。

translations.literal: The crown prince entrusted his young son Dayuan to Prince Yi of Xiangdong and also sent clipped fingernails and hair.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince entrusted his young son Dayuan to Prince Yi of Xiangdong and also sent clipped fingernails and hair as tokens.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙辰，上臥淨居殿，口苦，索蜜不得，再曰：「荷！

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingchen, the emperor lay ill in the Hall of Pure Dwelling; his mouth was bitter; he asked for honey and could not obtain it; twice he said, "Bitter!
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingchen, the emperor lay ill in the Hall of Pure Dwelling; his mouth was bitter; he asked for honey and could not obtain it; twice he said, "Bitter!

translations.literal: Bitter!
translations.idiomatic: Bitter!

translations.literal: " Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he died.

sentences.zh: 年八十六。

translations.literal: He was eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 景秘不發喪，遷殯於昭陽殿，迎太子於永福省，使如常入朝。

translations.literal: Jing secretly withheld announcement of the death, moved the coffin to Zhaoyang Hall, summoned the crown prince from Yongfu Palace, and had him enter court as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing secretly withheld announcement of the death, moved the coffin to Zhaoyang Hall, summoned the crown prince from Yongfu Palace, and had him enter court as usual.

sentences.zh: 王偉、陳慶皆侍太子，太子嗚咽流涕，不敢洩聲，殿外文武皆莫之知。

translations.literal: Wang Wei and Chen Qing both attended the crown prince; the prince sobbed with tears but dared not make a sound; civil and military officials outside the hall none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei and Chen Qing both attended the crown prince; the prince sobbed with tears but dared not make a sound; civil and military officials outside the hall knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 東魏高岳既失慕容紹宗等，志氣沮喪，不敢復逼長社城。

translations.literal: Gao Yue of Eastern Wei, having lost Murong Shaozong and the others, was dispirited and dared not press Changshe again.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue of Eastern Wei, having lost Murong Shaozong and the others, was dispirited and dared not press Changshe again.

sentences.zh: 陳元康言於大將軍澄曰：「王自輔政以來，未有殊功。

translations.literal: Chen Yuankang said to Grand General Cheng, "Your Highness, since assisting in government, has had no extraordinary achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuankang said to Grand General Cheng, "Your Highness, since assisting in government, has had no extraordinary achievement.

sentences.zh: 雖破侯景，本非外賊。

translations.literal: Though Hou Jing was defeated, he was never a foreign enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hou Jing was defeated, he was never a foreign enemy.

sentences.zh: 今穎川垂陷，願王自以為功。

translations.literal: Now Yingchuan is near falling; I wish Your Highness would make it your own achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yingchuan is near falling; I wish Your Highness would make it your own achievement.

sentences.zh: 」澄從之，戊寅，自將步騎十萬攻長社，親臨作堰。

translations.literal: " Cheng agreed; on wuyin he personally led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Changshe and personally oversaw building the dam.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng agreed; on wuyin he personally led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Changshe and personally oversaw building the dam.

sentences.zh: 堰三決，澄怒，推負土者及囊並塞之。

translations.literal: The dam broke three times; Cheng was angry and pushed those carrying earth and their bags together to fill the breach.
translations.idiomatic: The dam broke three times; Cheng was furious and drove earth-carriers and their bags together into the breach to fill it.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，發高祖喪，升梓宮於太極殿。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Gaozu's funeral was announced and the coffin was raised to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Emperor Wu's funeral was announced and the coffin was raised to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 是日，太子即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: That day the crown prince ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: That day the crown prince ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 侯景出屯朝堂，分兵守衛。

translations.literal: Hou Jing went out to camp at the Audience Hall and divided troops to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing went out to camp at the Audience Hall and posted guards throughout the palace.

sentences.zh: 壬午，詔北人在南為奴婢者，皆免之，所免萬計；

translations.literal: On renwu, an edict freed all northerners held as slaves and maidservants in the south; those freed numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, an edict freed all northerners held as slaves and maidservants in the south; those freed numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 景或更加超擢，冀收其力。

translations.literal: Jing sometimes further promoted them abruptly, hoping to win their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sometimes promoted them further still, hoping to win their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 高祖之末，建康士民服食、器用，爭尚豪華，糧無半年之儲，常資四方委輸。

translations.literal: At the end of Gaozu's reign, Jiankang gentry and commoners in dress, food, and utensils all vied in luxury; grain stores did not last half a year and always relied on deliveries from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Wu's reign, Jiankang gentry and commoners vied in luxury of dress, food, and furnishings; grain stores did not last half a year and always relied on deliveries from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 自景作亂，道路斷絕，數月之間，人至相食，猶不免餓死，存者百無一二。

translations.literal: Since Jing's rebellion, roads were cut; within months men came to eating one another, yet still could not escape starvation; of those who survived, not one or two in a hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hou Jing's rebellion, roads were cut; within months men came to eating one another, yet still could not escape starvation; scarcely one survivor in a hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 貴戚、豪族皆自出采穭，填委溝壑，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Nobles and powerful clans all went out themselves to gather wild grains; bodies filled gullies and ravines beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and powerful clans all went out themselves to gather wild grains; corpses filled gullies and ravines beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 癸未，景遣儀同三司來亮入宛陵，宣城太守楊白華誘而斬之。

translations.literal: On guimwei, Jing sent Lai Liang, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, into Wanling; Xuancheng Administrator Yang Baihua lured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei, Hou Jing sent Lai Liang, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, into Wanling; Xuancheng Administrator Yang Baihua lured and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，景遣其將李賢明攻之，不克。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Jing sent his general Li Xianming to attack but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Hou Jing sent his general Li Xianming to attack but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 景又遣中軍侯子鑒入吳郡，以廂公蘇單于為吳郡太守，遣儀同宋子仙等將兵東屯錢塘，新城戍主戴僧逖據縣拒之。

translations.literal: Jing again sent Central Army Commander Hou Zijian into Wu commandery, made Su Chanyu of the Secretariat Wu Administrator, and sent Song Zixian, Equal in Honor, and others east to camp at Qiantang; garrison commander Dai Sengti of Xincheng held the county and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing again sent Central Army Commander Hou Zijian into Wu commandery, made Su Chanyu of the Secretariat Wu Administrator, and sent Song Zixian and others east to camp at Qiantang; garrison commander Dai Sengti of Xincheng held the county and resisted.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞沈浚避難東歸，至吳興，太守張嵊與之合謀，舉兵討景。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Shen Jun fled eastward; reaching Wuxing, Administrator Zhang Sheng joined him in conspiracy and raised troops against Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Shen Jun fled eastward; reaching Wuxing, Administrator Zhang Sheng joined him in conspiracy and raised troops against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 嵊，稷之子也。

translations.literal: Sheng was Ji's son.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was Ji's son.

sentences.zh: 東揚州刺史臨城公大連，亦據州不受景命。

translations.literal: Eastern Yangzhou Inspector Duke Dalian of Lincheng also held the province and refused Jing's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yangzhou Inspector Duke Dalian of Lincheng also held the province and refused Hou Jing's orders.

sentences.zh: 景號令所行，唯吳郡以西、南陵以北而已。

translations.literal: Jing's orders took effect only west of Wu commandery and north of Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's orders took effect only west of Wu commandery and north of Nanling.

sentences.zh: 魏詔：「太和中代人改姓者皆復其舊。

translations.literal: A Wei edict: "Those who changed surnames in the Taihe era shall all restore their old ones.
translations.idiomatic: A Western Wei edict: "Those who changed surnames in the Taihe era shall all restore their old ones.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙戌，以南康王會理為侍中、司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingxu, Prince Huili of Nankang was made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingxu, Prince Huili of Nankang was made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，立宣城王大器為皇太子。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Prince Daqi of Xuancheng was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Prince Daqi of Xuancheng was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景將使太常卿南陽劉之遴授臨賀王正德璽綬，之遴剃髮僧服而逃。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hou Jing was about to have Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin of Nanyang invest Prince Zhengde of Linhe with seal and sash; Zhilin shaved his head, put on monk's robes, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hou Jing was about to have Minister of Ceremonies Liu Zhilin of Nanyang invest Prince Zhengde of Linhe with seal and sash; Zhilin shaved his head, put on monk's robes, and fled.

sentences.zh: 之遴博學能文，嘗為湘東王繹長史；

translations.literal: Zhilin was learned and literate and had once been chief administrator to Prince Yi of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilin was learned and literate and had once been chief administrator to Prince Yi of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 將歸江陵，繹素嫉其才，己丑，之遴至夏口，繹密送藥殺之，而自為志銘，厚其賻贈。

translations.literal: As he was returning to Jiangling, Yi had long envied his talent; on jichou, when Zhilin reached Xiakou, Yi secretly sent poison and killed him, then wrote his epitaph himself and gave generous funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: As he was returning to Jiangling, Yi had long envied his talent; on jichou, when Zhilin reached Xiakou, Yi secretly sent poison and killed him, then wrote his epitaph himself and gave generous funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，封皇子大心為尋陽王，大款為江陵王，大臨為南海王，大連為南郡王，大春為安陸王，大成為山陽王，大封為宜都王。

translations.literal: On renchen, the princes were enfeoffed: Daxin as Prince of Xunyang, Dakuan as Prince of Jiangling, Dalin as Prince of Nanhai, Dalian as Prince of Nan commandery, Dachun as Prince of Anlu, dacheng as Prince of Shanyang, and Dafeng as Prince of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, the princes were enfeoffed: Daxin as Prince of Xunyang, Dakuan as Prince of Jiangling, Dalin as Prince of Nanhai, Dalian as Prince of Nan commandery, Dachun as Prince of Anlu, Dacheng as Prince of Shanyang, and Dafeng as Prince of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 長社城中無鹽，人病攣腫，死者什八九。

translations.literal: Within Changshe there was no salt; people sickened with cramps and swelling; eight or nine in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Within Changshe there was no salt; people sickened with cramps and swelling; eight or nine in ten died.

sentences.zh: 大風從西北起，吹水入城，城壞。

translations.literal: A great wind rose from the northwest, blew water into the city, and the walls broke.
translations.idiomatic: A great wind rose from the northwest, blew floodwater into the city, and the walls gave way.

sentences.zh: 東魏大將軍澄令城中曰：「有能生致王大將軍者封侯；

translations.literal: Grand General Cheng of Eastern Wei proclaimed to the city, "Whoever can deliver General Wang alive shall be enfeoffed as a marquis;
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Gao Cheng of Eastern Wei proclaimed to the city, "Whoever can deliver General Wang alive shall be enfeoffed as a marquis;

sentences.zh: 若大將軍身有損傷，親近左右皆斬。

translations.literal: if General Wang's person suffers harm, all those close at hand shall be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: if General Wang's person suffers harm, all those close at hand shall be beheaded.

translations.idiomatic: " Wang Sizheng led his men to hold an earthen hill and told them, "My strength is spent and my plans exhausted—I can only repay the state with death!

translations.literal: " He then looked skyward and wailed, bowed twice toward the west, and meant to cut his own throat; commander Luo Xun said, "My lord often told Xun and the rest, 'You take my head and surrender—not only will you gain wealth and honor, you will also save a whole city of people.

sentences.zh: 』今高相既有此令，公獨不哀士卒之死乎！
